heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1S requires upgrading to a hardened steel nozzle and extruder gear before printing abrasive eSUN ePA-CF to prevent rapid mechanical wear. Once upgraded, the enclosed chamber provides an optimal thermal environment to reliably achieve speeds up to 131 mm/s at a capped volumetric flow rate of 11 mm³/s.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with PVP glue stick or liquid adhesive as an interface and release layer
slicerTweaks: Cap Maximum Volumetric Speed to 11 mm³/s in the filament settings to eliminate extrusion starvation at high feedrates.
Lower part cooling fan thresholds to 0% min and 20% max (with 0% for the first 3 layers) to maintain high interlayer bonding strength.
Set outer wall speed to 80 mm/s and inner wall speed to 120 mm/s to optimize surface finish and dimension consistency while staying below the 131 mm/s volumetric limit.
Enable Wipe While Retracting with a 1.0 mm wipe distance to minimize carbon fiber seam blobbing and z-seam stringing.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Intermittent under-extrusion and rapid nozzle orifice expansion
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Carbon fiber abrasive wear on the stock P1S stainless steel nozzle and extruder drive gears.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Replace the stock stainless hotend and extruder with official Bambu Lab hardened steel components.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe stringing, rough surface finish, and brittle layer adhesion
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Hydrolysis caused by high moisture absorption in the hygroscopic polyamide matrix.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament in an active blast oven or dry box at 70-80°C for at least 8 to 12 hours before printing directly from a dry enclosure.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Part warping and bed corner peeling
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Thermal contraction from chamber draft or excessive part cooling fan airflow.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Preheat the enclosed chamber by setting the bed to 85°C for 15 minutes, disable auxiliary fan, and apply a thin layer of glue stick on the textured PEI sheet.

faq.question: Can I print eSUN ePA-CF with the stock Bambu Lab P1S nozzle?
faq.answer: No, the stock P1S ships with a stainless steel nozzle and unhardened extruder gears, which eSUN ePA-CF will wear out within a single spool; install Bambu hardened steel replacements first.

faq.question: Do I need to keep the P1S door and top glass closed when printing eSUN ePA-CF?
faq.answer: Yes, keep the chamber fully closed to retain ambient heat and prevent ambient drafts, which helps reduce warping and maximizes layer adhesion in nylon.

faq.question: Is an AMS compatible with eSUN ePA-CF on the P1S?
faq.answer: While it can feed, continuous use of stiff, abrasive carbon fiber filament will groove standard AMS plastic funnels and Bowden tubes; external dry-box feeding is recommended for long-term reliability.

faq.question: What is the maximum printing speed I can use for eSUN ePA-CF?
faq.answer: Due to the 11 mm³/s maximum volumetric flow rate, standard 0.4mm nozzle lines at 0.2mm layer height are mechanically capped at 131 mm/s to ensure complete plasticization.
